parakeet: You can't drag God into the physical sandbox to claim credit for creation and then sprint into the hyperdimensional clouds the moment we ask to look at his hands. If the defense of transcendence fails, the focus usually shifts inward, blaming our own hardware. Human limitations prevent us from perceiving God directly. And be on the lookout because I have an entire video coming up exposing the hypocrisy of this admission. Now, on the surface, that sounds humble. In reality, it completely misses the point. There is an enormous list of things that human senses cannot perceive directly, like atoms, magnetic fields, radio waves, and dark energy. But our physical limitations have never prevented us from detecting their impact. We built tools to capture their footprints because those unseen things actively interact with our physical reality. And this is where the theology fractures under its own weight. Christianity is not claiming a completely detached, distant deistic deity who stays on his side of the fence. Christianity claims that a non-physical God explicitly interacted with physical reality to create a physical universe, shape physical human beings, and mold those human beings in his own image. This sets up an impossible riddle. How does a non-physical, non-detectable, non-embodied being create embodied creatures in its own image and then remain completely unavailable to the very physical model supposedly built to resemble it? Saying God is beyond human perception doesn't solve this riddle. It just adds more unpaid debt to the conversational ledger via another unverified claim. When an apologist gives this response, they're treating a stack of unverified assertions like an explanation. Before that stack can carry any logical weight, the believer is required to demonstrate a dizzying tower of claims.
